This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age reported) that investigates mental calculation tasks engaging working memory and manipulation (executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts of calculation versus active control conditions (result-matching, letter pseudo-calculation, substitution tasks). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms are described. Although the final analyzed sample is small (n=5) and a fixed-effects group model was used, these aspects do not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; phase-wise inhibition vs generation) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in SPM2 and presents voxelwise results (figures and Table 2 coordinates) with cluster-corrected thresholds. Relevant participant, modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60 years. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.
